2. The relevant fact giving rise to this Rule in short is that the opposite parties as plaintiffs instituted a suit for permanent injunction contending inter alia that after death of the R.S. recorded tenant Nabir Chandra Sheel his 2 brothers, namely, Shasthi Charan and Kali Charan have been owners of the suit land and the R.S khatian recorded in their names. Kali Charan died leaving his wife plaintiff No. 1 and 2 daughters, namely, shishu Bala and Paran Sona. Sishu Bala died leaving defendant Nos. 2 and 3 and Paran Sona died leaving plaintiff. The plaintiff Nos. 1-5 possess the suit land as homestead and garden and the plaintiffs possess the suit and described in 1 (ka) schedule to the plaint. The defendant is a rich man and terrorist in nature. The defendant had been threatening in venous way to dispossess the plaintiffs from the suit land of schedule No. 1 (ka). The plaintiffs brought this suit against the defendant not to disturb, dispossess, change the nature of the land and not to damage the garden of the suit land. Hence the suit. 

 3. The defendant contested the suit by filing written statement denying the material allegation made in the plaint contending inter alia that total 62 decimals of land under R.S. dag nos. 864,866 and 864/176 of R.S. khatian No. 745 belonged to Girls Chandra, Anatiga Mohan and Rajani Mohan sons of late Golak chandra and Shashti Charan, Kali Charan and Nabin Chandra sons of late Sarat chandra and R.S. khatian was recorded in their names. According to R. S. khatian they possess 51/5 decimals of land each in equal share. Girish chandra died leaving 2 sons, namely, Jatindra and Rabindra. Ananga Mohan died leaving 2 sons namely, Broza Hori and defendant No.1. Accordingly defendant No. 1 owned 5 decimals of land by inheritance. Giris Chandra, Rajani Mohan and Broza Hori sold to Sona Mi. and Nabin chandra vide 2 sale deeds being Nos. 1237 dated 16.5.1955 and 855 dated 21.6.1958. Above purchasers sold to defendant No. 1 vide kabala No. 1215 dated 24.4.1969 and they also sold to Rabindra and Broza Hori vide another kabala and defendant No. 1 became owner of 10 decimals of land. Kali Charan died in 1941 and Nabin Chandra died issueless leaving his brother Shasthi Charan as only heirs and total land of Shasthi Charan was 20 ½ decimals. Shasthi Charan sold 15½ decimals to Imam Sharif vide kabala No. 2362 dated 29.7.1952. Imam Sharif died leaving 2 sons, namely, Abul Hossain and Nabi Hossain who inherited the suit land. Abul Hossain and Nabi Hosain sold to defendant vide kabala No. 2012 dated 4.5.1987. Sashi charan died leaving his son, namely, Surondra Sheel who died leaving his sons Babul chandra. Babul Chandra sold 4½ decimals to defendant vide kabala No. 549 dated 25.2.1987. Kali Charms died leaving his wife Saira Bala and 2 daughters, namely, Shishu Bala and Paran Sona. Plaintiff No. 1 for her legal necesity sold 10% decimals land to Ananga Mohan father of the defendant vide kabala No. 3648 dated 17.12.1941. Ananga Mohan sold to one Mohan Bala and then Mohan Bala sold the same to one Abdul Ali and his son Abdus Sukur vide kabala 1940 dated 12.9.1974. Ali died leaving his son Abul Sukur who (Abdul shukur) sold 14 decimals of land to defendant on 19.5.1996 and accordingly the defendant has been owned 45½ decimals of land by way of purchase and inheritance. The rest of suit land of the schedule 17 decimals of land possessed by Genesis Chand, Braze Hori and Rabindra. Hence the suit is liable to be dismissed.
